notes:
WHAT THE PACKAGE IS: the card's main model (models[0], models/scene_g1.xml) served as a MujocoDriver in simulated R0 mode. The step action is data.ctrl bounded per actuator by the model's actuator_ctrlrange (29 position actuators; the position default sets inheritrange=1, so each range is its joint range), reset runs mj_resetData/mj_forward, the state is the bridge's world state {time_ms, qpos, qvel, ctrl, tick, timestep_ms, seed}, and the fidelity contract is F1 with lockstep clock and realtime_factor 0. The model file is read from the read-only clone in place; neither the model nor its assets are copied into the package and the upstream package is never imported. The gate passed on the fake backend with no failing findings. WHAT IS NOT COVERED: the LiDAR range image (one distance per ray, the same shape as the theta and phi arrays) and the point cloud that MjLidarWrapper.trace_rays produces; cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1 carry only the world state, so the scan, the scan patterns, the cpu/taichi/jax/warp backends, the cutoff distance and the sensor pose are not exposed by this package. No hardware is attached and no hardware run was made. THE FAKE: fake.py is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo. It parses the MJCF text (includes, default classes, actuator ranges, qpos/qvel layout) so the derived contract comes from the model, but its integration is a placeholder first-order motion of each actuated joint toward its control target; it loads no mesh or texture and resolves no contact, equality, tendon or sensor constraint. MuJoCo was not installed or importable where the gate ran (no network, no pip), so no trajectory was compared with the real engine and the sim backend path (real mujoco) was not run. EXPECTED WARNINGS: G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because backends['fake'] is the class object fake.FakeMujoco (a stand-in module, so the family records no native calls and exposes no fake surface to compare); G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived integer seed of reset, the numeric action.ctrl[*] of step and the integer ticks of step, which the bridge derives and PLAYBOOK section 8 lists as expected for simulator families. G4 reported no REF_VALUE or REF_BINARY warnings. This package is model-authored (driver.lock.json authored_by kind model, deepseek-v4.1-flash:1017, run wB2-210) and unreviewed (reviewed_by is null); nothing here was reviewed or tested by a human. test_driver.py keeps the check_driver call and adds six cases for the model shape, the per-actuator envelope, the state following the control target, reset to the model defaults, the published fidelity contract and the e-stop latch; those cases pass.
